gate: import torch, vllm, vllm._C — all three must import in the image's interpreter
voice_gate: import faster_whisper (the Ear) and at least one TTS engine (kokoro or chatterbox) in the same interpreter
torch_note: vllm._C is the compiled CUDA extension, so importing it proves the wheel matches this image's torch and CUDA. No private torch symbol is gated: torch.library does not export infer_schema in torch 2.4.x and vLLM never imports it, and requiring it rejected every candidate.
torch_label_note: The torch field is a LABEL, not a gate: the image's own torch is authoritative and the selector records what it actually imported (torch/torch_before_vllm) and warns when the label disagrees. The 2.4.0 base image ships torch 2.4.0+cu121 despite its cuda12.4.1 tag, which is what CI printed, so the label says so instead of claiming 2.4.1+cu124.

bases.torch_source: observed: CI build 44789927889 printed torch 2.4.0+cu121 in the gate
fallback base, never selected while the first base passes its gate

voice.transformers_note: Kokoro's warm-up failed on the transformers its TTS wheel pulled in. The in-container fix (4.47.1) only lasted as long as that container, so a fresh pod hit the same failure. The selector installs this pin AFTER the engines and re-imports the chosen engine, so the image carries the fix and proves it still loads.
voice.numpy_note: numpy 2.x is what pyarrow and datasets resolve against, but torch 2.4.x wheels were built against numpy 1.x, so the pin is installed LAST and then the whole stack is imported together in one interpreter: torch, vllm, vllm._C, transformers, faster-whisper, the chosen TTS engine and every optional extra (pyarrow/datasets) that already imported before the pin. A pin that fails that gate is rolled back to the numpy the image already had and recorded as numpy_source=rolled_back; extras that were already broken in the base image are recorded in numpy_extras and never counted against the pin.
